messages:
alex: Heads up — after runtime#4321 landed I’m seeing a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate on /v1/chat (prod-us). Hit rate went from ~62% -> ~19% for a 30s window during peak.
perf-bot: Automated profile: runtime#4321 changed kernel routing threshold. Observed kernel switch around seq=2048; result: token gen tail latency +18% and cache warmups doubled. snapshot: https://console.redwood/perf/1782
maya: repro steps? which client flags/headers were used when you captured this?
alex: Standard SDK (js) with default cache behavior. No explicit opt-out headers. Example request logged below.

alex: ```
POST /v1/chat/generate
Host: api.redwood.dev
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: r-7a2
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-7b",
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"..."},{"role":"user","content":"Explain KV caching"}],
  "stream": true
}
```

nathan: Interesting — runtime#4321 adjusted kernel-selection to prefer tiled kernels after seq>1536 for perf reasons. That change affects how we do prefix chunking and when KV cache is populated during the first stream chunks.

emma: So streaming + kernel switch -> warmup race? that could explain misses.
sarah: Any impact on retry behavior? customers reported duplicate warmups causing burst billing.

alex: Yes — noticed a client retry (429/backoff) triggered before prefix fully warmed. SDK retry loop re-sends streaming request with same prefex, which causes extra uncached work.

nathan: Quick mitigation: add a header to force client-side cache opt-in/opt-out while we investigate. Proposed header:

```
X-Redwood-Cache: opt-in     # client will use SDK prefix cache semantics (default behavior)
X-Redwood-Cache: opt-out    # bypass prefix cache for this request
```

emma: SDK change: expose cacheOptIn boolean and set X-Redwood-Cache automatically. Also add `cacheWarmupTimeoutMs` to control how long SDK waits for KV warmup on streaming before deciding to retry.

perf-bot: Metric delta: after temporarily toggling kernel-threshold back to 1536 in canary, hit-rate recovered to ~58% within 10 minutes. Reference: https://console.redwood/perf/1782/canary

alex: Action items:
- nathan: revert kernel-threshold to 1536 for rtp-canary and run 1h smoke
- emma: ship SDK patch to add X-Redwood-Cache and cacheWarmupTimeoutMs (opt-in default)
- maya: add alert on "prefix_cache_hit_rate < 30% over 5m"

nathan: I'll also add a short-term guard that disables kernel routing changes when stream=true and payload prefix_len < 2048 to avoid the warmup race.

deploy-bot: Deployer: scheduled canary rollback for runtime/pool-6 at 2026-03-17T14:40Z (job 7321)

sarah: Thanks — I'll notify affected customers and suggest setting `cacheOptIn=false` in SDK if they see duplicates until fix is GA.

alex: One more note: edge-case with partial-chunk flush — streaming sometimes sends a tiny first chunk which never triggers KV population. If SDK delays the first retry slightly (eg 120ms) we avoid duplicate cold starts. Add as low-priority tweak for SDK.

maya: great thread. tagging infra to watch GPU utilization during canary: @nathan please post perf snapshot after rollback.

nathan: Will do, posting updated perf link when available.
